data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Topical antibacterials & antiseptics_

**Class:** Iodophor (iodine complexed with polyvinylpyrrolidone)

## Mechanism of action
- Slowly releases free iodine → oxidises microbial proteins and nucleic acids → broad-spectrum killing of bacteria, fungi, viruses, spores

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Skin antisepsis before procedures, wound cleansing, infected ulcers, mouth gargle, vaginal antisepsis

## Dose & formulations
- 10% solution/5% scrub; allow 2 min contact and to dry; ointment once or twice daily on wounds

## Adverse effects
- Irritant dermatitis (especially under occlusion), allergic contact dermatitis (rare), skin staining
- Systemic iodine absorption from large wounds/neonates → hypothyroidism, metabolic acidosis, renal toxicity

## Contraindications
- Iodine allergy; thyroid disease (large areas); neonates and pregnancy (prolonged/large-area use)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid prolonged or large-area use (fetal/neonatal hypothyroidism).

## Viva points
- Needs contact time and drying; caution in neonates (hypothyroidism)

_Sources: Khopkar ch.30 (Povidone iodine); Wolverton 4e ch.54. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
